roomExtent.note: extent of everything baked (glTF Y-up metres); outside it there is nothing

notes: Units are metres, Y up (glTF). Meshes: room_shell (walls, ceiling, floor, mouldings, plaster rose, window frames, chimney piece), outside (the painted view behind the sash window: a card, treat it like any surface), furnishings (rug, armchair, table, plant, mantel props, print), shade_ribs, shade_fittings (lampholder, flex, black rose), bulb. Every mesh has one UV set (TEXCOORD_0) into the single shared 4096 atlas; there are no normals and no materials: draw all meshes unlit with the shader in hero.js that mixes hero_off.webp and hero_on.webp by a uniform; atlas colorSpace sRGB, flipY=false, no tone mapping (exposure, look, white balance, graduated gain and finishing are already in the pixels). No glazing is exported, so windows read clear; the gap where the second sash window (out of the usual frame) lets in only sky: use a pale blue clear colour (#D6E4F5 off, #2A3350 on). NOT baked, to approximate with CSS/canvas on top: vignette (post.*.vignette, centre post.*.vignette_centre as fractions from left/top: it darkens by that amount at the corners with an elliptical fall-off), bloom (post.on.bloom: a soft glow round hot highlights, i.e. the bulb at bulbCentre; use a radial sprite), grain. The page moves the camera with lookAt(target) by up to pointer.sideways_m / pointer.vertical_m; the bake covers a quarter more and aspect ratios 0.5 to 2.1 (wider and taller than 16:10 only at about half the texel density). Everything baked is matte-ish: specular highlights were baked from the surface normal, not the camera.
